takeaways: Components that do the same thing across a set of pages are identified the same way: same label, same icon, same accessible name.
Consistent does not mean identical text every time. “Go to page 4” and “Go to page 5” are consistent.
Text alternatives count. A search icon is “Search” on every page, not “Find” on one and “Look up” on another.
It is about naming. The order of repeated navigation is 3.2.3, and matching visible and coded labels is 2.5.3.
failures: “Save” on one screen and “Done” on another for the same action
Two different icons for the same function
An icon button with a different hidden label on each page
check: List every repeated action and its label, icon and accessible name across screens.
Look for the same function with different words or icons.
Check icon-only buttons’ accessible names, not just their visuals.

quiz.question: Saving changes is “Save” in the editor, “Done” in settings, and a floppy disk icon in the profile. What is the fix?
options: None. Each page is consistent with itself
Choose one label and icon and use it everywhere
Add tooltips that explain each version
quiz.why: The function is the same, so its identity should be too. Tooltips explain the inconsistency without removing it.

spec: Keep a list of shared actions with their label, icon and accessible name.
Annotate icon-only buttons with the exact accessible name.
Flag any place where a familiar action is named differently on purpose, and why.
review: Is this the same action we call something else elsewhere?
Does this icon mean the same thing on every screen?
What will a screen reader say for this button here, and on the other pages?
tradeoff: Different teams and contexts pull toward local wording. Agree on one name per function, and allow small variations only when the function itself is different.
system: Put shared actions in the component library with fixed labels, icons and accessible names, and keep a content glossary.
pitch: If “Save” has three names, people have to learn our product three times. One name per action makes it easier for everyone.
